facts.claim: Daylesford is about an hour and a half north-west of Melbourne, with many spas, food and wine, artists and holistic therapists.
It has the highest concentration of natural mineral springs in Australia; free mineral spring taps around town dispense essentially untreated water.
Founded in 1852 as a gold mining town; population 2,781 at the 2021 census; one of Australia's few spa towns.
Wombat Hill Botanic Gardens is on the Victorian Heritage Register; Lake Daylesford is a popular walk and picnic site; Convent Gallery spreads art over three storeys of a 19th-century mansion.
Hepburn Springs, 3 km north, sits in the middle of Australia's largest concentration of mineral springs and has Swiss-Italian heritage.
Town centre is small and walkable but sights outside it need a car or bike; it is steep for cycling.

experiences: Soak in natural mineral springs and spas
Taste mineral spring water straight from the tap
Wander lakeside and botanic garden paths

tips.title: Bring a car
tips.detail: Only one V/Line coach stop serves town, and most sights, springs and farms are well apart. A car or bike is needed beyond the centre; it is steep.

tips.title: Mineral taps are untreated
tips.detail: Free mineral spring taps around town are tested often, but the water is essentially untreated. Taste a little before filling a big container.

tips.title: Book bathhouses ahead
tips.detail: Spa bathhouses are the main reason to visit and many double as accommodation. Book treatments before you arrive, especially for weekends.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED seasonal guide not found in fetched sources; Wikipedia gives mean max 15.5C, min 7.0C and 882 mm rain a year, so cool and wet: spa weather is year-round, mild autumn and spring chosen. Owner to confirm.

facts.claim: Torquay is the official start of the Great Ocean Road, 21 km south of Geelong, and a surfing hub where Rip Curl, Quiksilver and Billabong set up shop; it had 18,534 people at the 2021 census.
The Australian National Surfing Museum in Torquay is described as the largest surfing museum in the world.
Bells Beach hosts the Rip Curl Pro, the world's longest continuously running pro surfing competition, held at Easter every year since 1962 (first held January 1962).
Anglesea is where the Great Ocean Road first meets the ocean; its golf course is known for resident eastern grey kangaroos, and its population peaks around Christmas and New Year.
Aireys Inlet has a 19th-century lighthouse still in operation; the timber-log Great Ocean Road Memorial Arch commemorates returned soldiers who built the road (begun 1919, fully opened 1932).
Torquay Surf Beach and Point Danger/Zeally Bay are the town's coastal features.

experiences: Surf or watch surfers at famous breaks
Drive the start of the Great Ocean Road
Spot kangaroos on the golf course

tips.title: Check surf before Bells
tips.detail: Bells Beach is a serious surf break; swell and wind decide whether it works. Winki Pop nearby often works in more varied conditions.

tips.title: Summer is crowded
tips.detail: Anglesea and the coast fill with Melbourne holidaymakers around Christmas and New Year. Book stays well ahead or visit outside that peak.

tips.title: Train to Geelong, then car
tips.detail: Trains from Melbourne's Southern Cross run to Geelong every 30-40 minutes, then rent a car or bus to Torquay, the start of the road.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED: sources show summer crowds peaking Christmas-New Year and the Rip Curl Pro at Easter; swim/beach season summer into autumn. Owner to confirm with a tourism source.

seasonal_tags: Rip Curl Pro at Bells Beach every Easter (recurring; a pattern, not a promise for any visit)
wikivoyage_page: no (https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Surf_Coast is an empty page, 404); Torquay has one: https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Torquay_(Victoria)

facts.claim: Bright is a town in north-eastern Victoria at 319 m above sea level at the south-eastern end of the Ovens Valley; population 2,620 at the 2021 census.
Tourism is the main industry, with focus on the autumn colours of European trees planted in the area, and the Bright Autumn Festival as a major cultural event.
It is a major gateway to alpine scenery near Mount Buffalo National Park, Mount Feathertop and Mount Hotham; Mount Bogong (1,986 m) is Victoria's highest peak.
Many paragliding and hang glider launch sites lie close to Bright; the town hosts paragliding competitions.
Gold rush history: Chinese miners reworked abandoned claims; the Ovens River was dredged clean by the 1950s. The old rail line is now a rail trail to Wangaratta.
Bright is about 3.5 hours from Melbourne and 1.5 hours from Albury-Wodonga; most visitors come by road.

experiences: See autumn colours along the river
Cycle rail trails and riverside paths
Launch a paraglider or hang glider
Use Bright as a base for the Victorian Alps

tips.title: Autumn is busiest
tips.detail: Autumn colours and the Bright Autumn Festival draw crowds; many houses are holiday rentals, so book accommodation well ahead.

tips.title: Allow for the drive
tips.detail: About 3.5 hours from Melbourne by road; public transport is limited to V/Line buses connecting at Seymour (once daily on weekends).

tips.title: River water is cold
tips.detail: Spring and summer swimming on the Ovens River is popular, but the water is very cold, so test it before going in.

best_months.rationale: Autumn colour (Mar-May) is the town's signature draw; summer is a popular family season with warm sunny days and swimming; winter is ski season at nearby resorts.

wikivoyage_page: yes (as 'Bright', not 'Bright (Victoria)', which is empty) https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Bright

facts.claim: Wine-growing region about an hour's drive from Melbourne CBD via the Maroondah Highway, with more than 80 wineries; known for cool-climate Chardonnay and Pinot Noir and sparkling wine.
Healesville Sanctuary is a wildlife park with rehabilitation facilities, breeding programmes for endangered species and education for visitors.
TarraWarra Museum of Art holds early Modernist Australian paintings with sweeping views of the TarraWarra vineyards.
The Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail is a 40 km track on an old railway line for cyclists, walkers and horse riders.
The first vineyards were planted in the 1830s, making it one of Australia's oldest wine industries.
Yarra Valley Railway runs from Healesville on weekends and public holidays; Yarra Glen has a Sunday market.

experiences: Taste cool-climate wines at cellar doors
Cycle the Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail

tips.title: Public transport is patchy
tips.detail: Train to Lilydale then bus 685 reaches Yarra Glen, TarraWarra and Healesville. For multiple cellar doors, hire a driver or tour and never drink and drive.

tips.title: Check weekend-only railway
tips.detail: Yarra Valley Railway at Healesville runs only on weekends and public holidays, and Yarra Glen's market is on Sundays.

tips.title: Take the train, then cycle
tips.detail: Catch the train to Lilydale and ride the 40 km rail trail to Warburton for a car-free day in the valley.

best_months.rationale: UNVERIFIED: no fetched source gives a seasonal guide. Autumn vintage and spring chosen for cool-climate wine touring; owner to confirm with a tourism source.
